productDefects: Remote external-agent inventory relied on a fixed startup delay instead of receiver-driven snapshot and reconnect ordering.
Captured directory environments replayed PROMPT_COMMAND without its non-exported shell function, producing an immediate broken prompt.
Remote Vim shell commands inherited the remote home directory rather than the opened project cwd.
TCP DAP accepted an SSH forward before the remote adapter owned the destination, allowing a reset connection to become the session transport.
testHarnessDefects: Live TCP port allocation sent python -c source to SSH without one remote-shell quoting boundary.
ACP project evidence was incorrectly required to coexist in one tool call instead of the union of completed calls.
The terminal UAT fixture returned from signal.pause after SIGWINCH instead of remaining alive for Ctrl-C.
processDefects: Earlier release acceptance sampled components and marker responses without executing every changed assembled-product surface and user journey.
fixedDuringRun: Replaced fixed-delay external-agent inventory with request/response snapshots, rejoin refresh, and stale-response suppression.
Added a RED SSH argv-shape regression and one shell-quoted remote command.
Added a RED split-tool-evidence fixture and unioned only completed tool evidence.
Kept the terminal fixture alive across resize until the intended interrupt.
Removed captured PROMPT_COMMAND before explicit terminal or task settings are applied.
Anchored remote Vim shell execution to the opened project directory.
Rejected reset TCP-forward connections during a bounded stability probe and retried the adapter connection.
Retained marker-only, prompt-echo, permission, timeout, and cleanup negatives.
newInformationSummary: The installed e153 remote server advertises both secure environment capabilities and passes real noninteractive, PTY, and TCP journeys.
Zed 10x opens the populated Intrepid checkout and terminal/task processes inherit exact cwd, directory/surface environment, input, resize, interrupt, and cleanup behavior.
Installed Vim, MCP, DAP stdio, and DAP TCP journeys run from the real project and complete their actual protocol or editor behavior.
Real ACP agents may establish cwd and digest through different completed tool calls.
Codex Mac primary and Intrepid GLM each complete a withheld-oracle project read with no approved permission request.
residualRisk: Public notarized distribution is intentionally out of scope; the installed private app uses a verified ad-hoc signature.
The exact merged commit still requires a fresh post-merge bundle/install and focused repeat canary; the current installed binary identifies the pre-merge candidate.
